findings.observation: The original cached-500 and pruned-key examples were attributed to Stripe without the API v1 qualification.
findings.consequence: An agent could apply the v1 response replay example to a v2 endpoint despite different documented behavior.
findings.correction: Qualified the original response and pruning examples as API v1; preserved indeterminate-outcome recovery and the prohibition on escaping uncertainty with a fresh key.

findings.observation: Current provider documentation distinguishes v2 replay behavior and key scope from v1.
findings.consequence: A same-key v2 retry can yield an updated result, and its window cannot safely be transferred to v1.
findings.correction: Added a compact v2 contrast with same API, account/sandbox and 30-day conditions; endpoint namespace is separate from SDK version.

findings.observation: Generic provider/version inspection did not identify the concrete request artifacts that select these different contracts.
findings.consequence: Provider name or SDK version alone can select the wrong replay policy.
findings.correction: Require actual method/path, account/sandbox and API-version evidence from wiring/configuration or redacted requests; test sent key/scope through retry and restart without treating a mock as provider proof.

commonFixtures.project-context.md: Review fixture, not an executable integration. Java 17 application; existing HTTP adapter sends POST requests. The request body's bytes are omitted from the capture for privacy, but the original valid body and semantic fingerprint are durably stored and available to the recovery worker. The worker resends the original method, URL, account, key and body. Local operation records persist for 45 days. The product requires one account-creation intent and eventual outcome reporting; it does not promise byte-identical response replay. No provider calls are authorized.

captured-request.json.bodyHandling: original valid request bytes retained unchanged by the adapter; capture redacted

commonFixtures.provider-contracts.md:
Source snapshots for this review, consulted 2026-10-16. They describe provider contracts, not an observation that this particular operation succeeded.

Stripe API v1: an executed keyed POST records its first response, including a server error; repeats return that saved result. Server errors can accompany unresolved effects. A removed key no longer protects the old operation. Sources: https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests and https://docs.stripe.com/error-low-level#server-errors.

Stripe API v2: failed or partially failed work can be attempted again; previously successful changes are not repeated and replies can update. Replay matching includes the key, API, account/sandbox and a 30-day window. Source: https://docs.stripe.com/api-v2-overview#idempotency.

Both namespaces can occur in one integration. Their selection is visible in the URL path, separate from the date-based Stripe-Version header.
commonFixtures.recovery-note.md: Current proposal: Stripe caches every 500 forever. Return that error for every subsequent recovery attempt, mark the business operation REJECTED, and delete the operation record so users can submit again.
